Stated Claim / Post Context:
Trump, Xi and Putin plan unprecedented joint meeting

The leaders of the United States, China and Russia are set to meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China.

Actual Article Body:

The leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet on the sidelines of next week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen — an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world's biggest nuclear powers.

Plans for the three-way summit with Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin have been confirmed by the White House. It comes at a complicated moment in relations between the three countries.

Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the US war with Iran and other tensions between the world's foremost economic powers.

Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin, even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly 5-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.

The US president has insisted that such a meeting would provide an opportunity for the three leaders to discuss the US war with Iran and his goal of reaching a three-way agreement on their nuclear arms stockpiles.

The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for "a new, improved and modernised" deal that includes China.

But Beijing's arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the US and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With US and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.

By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China's growing clout and prestige.

For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.

The trilateral could very well overshadow the APEC summit. which is bringing 21 economies to Shenzhen, China's coastal metropolis that's transformed into a global technology and economic hub in just a few decades.
